messages:

Cc: NovumHealth Procurement <procurement@novumhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Request: mid-contract capacity add + early-renewal credit?

Hi Jonas —

We had a usage spike this month and need to add ~200k tokens/month for the next 9 months. We are mid-contract (ends May 2026) and procurement is asking whether Redwood will entertain a partial committed add now and an early renewal incentive (credit) if we agree to an earlier co-term/annualize at the next renewal.

Couple of constraints from our side:
- PO needs to be issued by 12/10 to hit finance cutoff.
- We prefer a single invoice schedule if possible (quarterly or annual) but can accept monthly billing if needed.
- We’d like to understand the net dollar impact vs pay-as-you-go and whether an accelerated credit is available for committing earlier.

Can you share a couple of concrete paths (pro-rata top-up, staged commit with credit, invoice timing)? I can loop procurement/finance if helpful — I’ve CC’d them.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Director, Platform Engineering
NovumHealth

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Elena Soto <elena@novumhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract capacity add + early-renewal credit?

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask. Below are three pragmatic options; I’ve looped Marissa (commercial) and Ben (rev ops) to confirm invoicing mechanics.

Option 1 — Pro-rata top-up (no change to contract)
- Add 200k tokens/mo immediately; charge pro-rata for remainder of current term (through May 2026).
- Invoiced monthly.
- No early-renewal credit.
- Fastest to implement.

Option 2 — Staged commit + accelerator (recommended if you want a credit)
- Add a committed 200k tokens/mo for the next 12 months starting now.
- We apply a 6% accelerator credit on committed spend if you sign an early co-term (annualize at invoice date) and accept 12-month billing cadence.
- Billing: quarterly invoices (option) or a single annual invoice (preferred for PO simplicity).

Option 3 — Hybrid bridge + renewal credit
- Immediate pro-rata top-up through 2/28/2026, then convert to a 12-month commit with a 7% credit if renewal is executed before 2/1/2026.
- Slightly more complex but gives a short runway for internal approvals.

Things we need from you:
- Which option you prefer (1/2/3)
- Target invoice cadence (monthly / quarterly / annual)
- PO timeline and who in procurement is the signer

I’m attaching a short procurement worksheet that maps the incremental cost for each option. If you want, Marissa can put a formal amendment in DocuSign with exact pricing.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi Elena —

Following Jonas’s note, we put together a clean amendment you can share with procurement. Summary below:

- Amendment: Add 200k committed tokens/month (12-month term) starting 12/15/2025.
- Credit: 6% accelerator credit on total committed spend if Novum executes the amendment and elects a 12-month billing cadence (quarterly or annual invoice) by 12/10/2025.
- Billing options we can support: quarterly in arrears (default), or single annual invoice (requires advance PO).
- Cancellation/true-up: standard pro-rata true-up at the end of the committed term.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
1) Novum confirms option 2 and billing cadence by 12/06.
2) Redwood sends DocuSign amendment (we’ll pre-fill with PO/Contact fields) by 12/07.
3) Novum returns signed amendment and PO by 12/10.
4) We activate committed capacity on 12/15.

I attached the amendment draft (v3) and the procurement sheet Jonas referenced. Ben — can you confirm we can accept a single annual invoice for this deal if they provide PO in advance?

Elena — if that timeline is tight we can also implement Option 3 (bridge) — let me know which you prefer and I’ll push DocuSign ASAP.

Thanks,
